messages:
pavel: Heads-up — ran an nsys trace on the dedicated pool after r2345 flip. Perfetto/qdrep attached. Seeing a spike around 2s where kernel selector chooses matmul_v2 instead of matmul_fused, and matmul_v2 path does an extra host->device memcpy which looks like the perf regression. https://perfetto.link/abc123 and s3://redwood-traces/1765432100/nsys.qdrep

maya: Wait, did r2345 change selector heuristics? I remember updating sequence-length thresholds but shouldn’t affect kernel choice this drastically.

jun: I changed the batching heuristic earlier but didn’t touch kernel selector. I can bisect. Can someone share the minimal repro (model + seq_len) + the exact nsys flags you used? @perf-bot can you provision the job?

perf-bot: autometrics: scheduled trace job t-8421 for commit range r2341..r2345. nvprof/nsys artifacts will be uploaded to s3://redwood-traces/1765432100/ when complete.

pavel: repro: small-llm-7b, seq_len=1200, batch=1 (this reproduces in ~2s). nsys command I used:

```
nsys profile -o out.qdrep --trace=nvtx,cuda python -m bench.run --model small-llm-7b --seq_len 1200 --batch 1 --warmup 5 --iter 10
```

sam: did a quick before/after diff (r2340 vs r2345) on a parallel run. Heatmap shows matmul_v2 invocation count up ~4x and device memcpy time up ~2x on the slow run. The timeline has memcpy immediately after kernel launch in 60% of calls. Looks like a prefetch/populate path is hitting the host staging buffer.

maya: I can reproduce locally with the same flags. Perfetto timeline shows a host memcpy in the kernel wrapper boundary — suspicious that the kernel wrapper introduced a fallback codepath that moves KV prefetch to host staging when certain alignment flags are set.

jun: Bisect plan: run quick nsys headless on GPU-qa for commits r2341..r2345 (parallel 3-at-a-time) using the command above but with --iter 3 to speed up. I'll start runs in ~20m. If someone can shorten model to 1-layer toy to get faster iterations, DM me the config.

pavel: uploaded a quick flame screenshot (s3://redwood-traces/1765432100/flame.png). Also logs from the runtime around selection: 

``[2026-03-18T15:12:03Z] kernel_selector: chosen=matmul_v2 reason='cost_model:fast_when_long_seq' fallback_policy='memcopy_prefetch'``

sam: If bisect signals matmul_v2 wrapper, I can prototype a guard to avoid host memcpy when KV cache state is 'ready' and test perf impact. @maya can you add a small integration test toggling prefetch flags so we catch regressions?

maya: :thumbsup: I'll add an integration test to eng-runtime CI that toggles prefetch and asserts no host memcpy shows up in perfetto for the long-seq path. Will tag @jun once it's in.

jun: thanks — I'll post bisect results in this thread. If anyone sees a faster repro or wants to run a candidate patch, ping me and I’ll share the QA GPU slots.
